notes: The relational argument avoids the documented pitfall, but the final inference requires V_{n+2}[z] to be a neighborhood, which no hypothesis guarantees. Take X={0}∪{1/k:k≥1} with its usual subspace topology, well-ordered as 0≺1≺1/2≺⋯, and V_m=Δ_X for every m. All stated hypotheses hold and A_n(x)={x}, yet every neighborhood of 0 meets infinitely many members of AA_n. An arbitrary set containing z and meeting at most one member does not establish discreteness.
